results.name: Dumbbell Decline Close Neutral Grip Press
instructions: Lie back on a decline bench with your feet firmly planted. Hold a dumbbell in each hand close together above your chest using a neutral grip.
Bend your elbows and lower the dumbbells toward your chest while keeping your palms facing each other and your elbows close to your torso.
Press both dumbbells upward together until your arms are extended directly above your chest without locking your elbows.
Slowly lower the dumbbells along the same path until they return close to your chest, then repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep your elbows tucked close to your torso as you lower the weights.
Press the dumbbells directly above your chest without letting them drift toward your head.
Maintain contact between your head, back, hips, and the bench throughout the exercise.
Inhale as you lower the dumbbells and exhale as you press them upward.
results.description: Dumbbell Decline Close Neutral Grip Press is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Forearms.

results.name: Dumbbell Fly Flat Bench Slow
instructions: Begin by lying on a flat bench with your feet flat on the floor for stability. Hold a dumbbell in each hand with your arms extended straight above your chest, palms facing each other.
Slowly lower the dumbbells out to your sides in a wide arc, maintaining a slight bend in your elbows. Lower until your upper arms are parallel to the floor or slightly below chest level.
Slowly bring the dumbbells back up to the starting position by squeezing your chest muscles, keeping the slight bend in your elbows throughout the movement.
tips: Avoid allowing the dumbbells to touch at the top to maintain tension in the chest muscles.
Keep your feet flat on the floor to provide stability and support.
Ensure your wrists remain straight and aligned with your forearms.
results.description: Dumbbell Fly Flat Bench Slow is an intermediate single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders.

results.name: Dumbbell Fly Incline Bench
instructions: Lie down on an incline bench with your feet flat on the floor. Hold a dumbbell in each hand and lie back on the bench with your arms extended straight above your chest, palms facing each other.
Slowly lower the dumbbells out to your sides in a wide arc, maintaining a slight bend in your elbows. Lower until your upper arms are parallel to the floor or slightly below chest level.
Bring the dumbbells back up to the starting position by squeezing your chest muscles, keeping the slight bend in your elbows throughout the movement.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, maintaining control and proper form throughout the exercise.
tips: Avoid allowing the dumbbells to touch at the top to maintain tension in the chest muscles.
Keep your feet flat on the floor to provide stability and support.

results.name: Dumbbell Hex Press
instructions: Lie on a flat bench with your feet firmly on the floor. Hold two dumbbells together above the center of your chest with your palms facing each other and your elbows bent.
Press the dumbbells upward while squeezing them firmly together until your arms are extended.
Pause briefly at the top while keeping the dumbbells pressed together and your chest engaged.
Bend your elbows and lower the dumbbells toward your chest with control, then repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep your elbows close to your torso as you lower the dumbbells.
Focus on squeezing your chest as you press the dumbbells upward.
Lower the dumbbells slowly without bouncing them against your chest.
Inhale as you lower the dumbbells and exhale as you press them upward.
results.description: Dumbbell Hex Press is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Forearms.

results.name: Flat Bench Cable Fly
instructions: Position a flat bench between two cable machines with the pulleys set at the lowest position. Attach handles to the pulleys and lie down on the bench with your feet flat on the floor.
Grasp the handles with both hands, palms facing up, and extend your arms out to your sides at chest level.
Raise the handles over your chest in a wide arc, keeping a slight bend in your elbows, squeezing your chest at the top.
Slowly bring the handles back to the starting position with control. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep a slight bend in your elbows throughout the movement to avoid straining your joints.
Focus on engaging your chest muscles throughout the movement.
Inhale as you lower the handles back down and exhale as you raise them up.
results.description: Flat Bench Cable Fly is a beginner single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with a cable, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Biceps.

results.name: Floor Cable Resistance Band Press
instructions: Lie on the floor with your knees bent and feet flat on the floor. Position a resistance band under your upper back, holding a handle in each hand with your palms facing forward.
Position your elbows on the floor bent at a 90-degree angle.
Press the handles straight up towards the ceiling until your arms are fully extended, keeping a slight bend in your elbows.
Slowly return to the starting position with control. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Exhale as you press the handles up and inhale as you return them to the starting position.
Use a lighter resistance band if needed to ensure proper form and gradually increase the resistance as you get stronger.
Focus on engaging your chest muscles throughout the movement.
results.description: Floor Cable Resistance Band Press is a beginner multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with a cable, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Triceps.

results.name: Hammer Strength MTS Iso-Lateral Decline Press Alternating Arms
instructions: Sit on the Hammer Strength MTS Iso-Lateral Decline Press, back pressed against the backrest and feet flat on the floor. Grasp the handles with both hands, palms facing down.
Press one handle forward by extending your arm, keeping the other arm stationary.
Squeeze your chest muscles at the bottom of the movement and slowly return the handle to the starting position with control.
Repeat with the other arm, alternating arms for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Exhale as you press the handle and inhale as you return it to the starting position.
Keep your back pressed against the backrest throughout the exercise.
Focus on engaging your chest muscles throughout the movement.
results.description: Hammer Strength MTS Iso-Lateral Decline Press Alternating Arms is a beginner multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with a leverage machine, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Triceps.
